text:
maria: Thinking out loud — propose we split the current onboarding validator into two orthogonal stages: a lightweight preflight (fast checks + microbench) and a full admission run (end-to-end bench + contract tests). keeps PR turnaround fast while preserving safety for prod commits.

dan: +1 on split. whats the exact boundary? preflight should be <5m total and not run heavy perf sweeps.

maria: boundary idea: preflight validates model metadata, tokenizer sanity, basic forward pass on 1..3 sequence lengths, and a small latency microbench (10 inferences). returns a compact "compatibility vector" metadata blob.

kai: compatibility vector = nice. what fields? I'm thinking: {arch, dtypes, kv_shapes, kv_shardable, tokenizer_id, seq_presets, quant_support, expected_gpu_mem_bytes, perf_micro_qps}. store as structured tags so routing/runtime can pick fallback variants.

maria: exactly. wire-format could be a tiny JSON with stable keys. keep stable for 2 major versions.

dan: for preflight do we run on the same hardware matrix as infra? e.g., A100-80GB vs T4 — or do we keep it generic? preflight shouldn't be too environment specific.

nate: preflight should run on a single canonical runner (small node type we control). full admission runs the multihardware sweep in the bench infra and writes telemetry bundles to s3 (bench artifacts).

sophia: UX: if preflight passes but admission fails, we should tag the model as "staged-failed" and surface the bench artifacts link in the console with suggested fixes. avoid silent fallout.

kai: contract tests — want them to be protobuf-defined tests that runtime implements. eg: max_output_length, permissive_tokenizer_checks, kv-cache-consistency. these should run in both stages but lighter in preflight (smoke).

maria: tradeoff: running contract tests in preflight increases false negatives, but not running them increases surprise in admission. propose smoke-run of contract tests in preflight (single seed). full set in admission.

dan: how do we fail fast vs flake? bench noise can cause spurious failures. we should use comparison windows and % delta thresholds. e.g., fail admission if perf regression >7% median across replicated runs. for accuracy/regression tests, fail if >2% absolute drop on tracked eval sets.

nate: implement statistical guard: run 3 repeats for each workload in admission, compute median, and compare. store raw samples in artifact bundle.

kai: compatibility vector needs a version field to avoid downstream breakage when we add new keys. also include hashed schema id.

sophia: ops question: how will rollout wire up with the console/rollouts page? we need model flags: admitted, staged, blocked, partial-admit. console should show the compatibility vector and bench summary at-a-glance.

maria: agree. also add "fallback_recommendations" in vector: e.g., suggest lower-quant variant, smaller seq, or slow-path CPU fallback.

dan: API suggestions: /validate/preflight POST -> returns {ok, vector_url, quick_logs, warnings}. /validate/admit POST -> returns {ok, admission_id, artifacts_url, metrics_summary}. both idempotent.

kai: add /validate/status?admission_id=... for async polling. and webhooks for infra to push completion events to the console.

nate: infra concerns: admission bench is heavy. we should cost-tag each admission and only run full admission for models that hit a usage threshold or explicit "request admission" flag. otherwise they stay in "limited" mode.

sophia: we need a clear developer path: fast preflight on PR -> dev sees vector -> optionally request admission -> lab-run will run full bench and provide signoff. docs should show sample vector and common failures.

dan: implementation detail: preflight runner should be containerized, lightweight, and share the same validator code but with a configurable profile. we can reuse the current validator service with a "--fast-profile" flag. avoids duplicate code.

kai: long-term refactor idea: split validator into "validator-core" (pure checks + rules) and "runner" (env-specific harness). validator-core can be imported by other tools (console, CLI) — reduces duplication.

maria: I like core + runner. core exposes a stable python API: validate_metadata(), run_contract_smoke(), microbench(). runner handles orchestration, retries, artifact upload.

nate: will need a migration plan for existing model records. propose: run a retroactive preflight sweep for active models to backfill compatibility_vector. schedule low-priority jobs over 2 weeks.

sophia: make sure owner notification goes out if retro preflight finds issues. owner field is mandatory at intake.

dan: question on quantization/serialized artifacts: should admission require uploaded quantized artifacts or will we generate them?

maria: prefer: admission accepts an artifact bundle (optional). if none provided, bench infra will attempt a best-effort quantization pass (cpu-based) but mark results as "generated" and require owner approval before auto-rolling into prod.

kai: add a flag in vector: quant_artifact_present: true|false and quant_profile: "int8-llm", "tf32-fp16" etc.

nate: logging: include a small artifact index file with checksums and a bench.summary.json. bench runner should upload: raw_samples.tar.gz, bench.summary.json, vector.json, contract_test_logs.txt.

sophia: decisions for MVP:
  1) implement preflight + admission split
  2) compatibility_vector schema v1 with fields kai proposed
  3) API endpoints: /validate/preflight, /validate/admit, /validate/status
  4) runner flag --fast-profile to reuse existing validator
  5) retrospective preflight for active models
  6) console surfaces vector + artifacts link and clear owner notification

maria: can someone drive a short RFC doc with schema proto and API shapes? I can start a skeletal doc. who wants to own the validator-core refactor?

dan: I'll own validator-core refactor. will sketch module boundaries and a migration plan.

kai: I'll write the vector schema proto and example JSON.

nate: infra: I'll size runner capacity and add cost tags for admission jobs.

sophia: I'll draft the console UX and the owner notification flow.

maria: thanks. next sync: Friday 10am to review RFC. posting checklist in #eng-ml-rfcs. :thumbsup: 

ops-bot: deploy-notice: bench-runner-v2 image pushed to staging at sha:abc123, scheduled for canary at 11:00.
